title.raw: 卷17 明元六王 Volume 17: Emperor Mingyuan's Six Princes

sentences.zh: 明元皇帝七男。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingyuan had seven sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan had seven sons.

sentences.zh: 杜密皇后生世祖太武皇帝。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Du Mi gave birth to Shizu Emperor Taiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Du bore Shizu Emperor Taiwu.

sentences.zh: 大慕容夫人生樂平戾王丕。

translations.literal: Lady Da Murong gave birth to Prince Pi of Leping, posthumously styled the Ill-Fated King.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Da Murong bore Prince Pi of Leping, who received the posthumous title Ill-Fated King.

sentences.zh: 安定殤王彌闕母氏。

translations.literal: Prince Mi of Anding, posthumously styled the Early-Deceased King — his mother's name is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mi of Anding, posthumously styled the Early-Deceased King, is of unknown maternity.

sentences.zh: 慕容夫人生樂安宣王範。

translations.literal: Lady Murong gave birth to Prince Fan of Le'an, posthumously styled the Proclaiming King.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Murong bore Prince Fan of Le'an, who received the posthumous title Proclaiming King.

sentences.zh: 尹夫人生永昌莊王健。

translations.literal: Lady Yin gave birth to Prince Jian of Yongchang, posthumously styled the Magnificent King.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin bore Prince Jian of Yongchang, who received the posthumous title Magnificent King.

sentences.zh: 建寧王崇、新興王俊二王，並闕母氏。

translations.literal: The two princes, Chong of Jianning and Jun of Xinxing, both lack recorded mothers.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes Chong of Jianning and Jun of Xinxing both have unrecorded mothers.

sentences.zh: 樂平王丕，少有才幹，為世所稱。

translations.literal: Pi, Prince of Leping, had talent and ability from youth and was praised by his generation.
translations.idiomatic: Pi, Prince of Leping, had talent and ability from youth and was praised by his generation.

sentences.zh: 太宗以丕長，愛其器度，特優異之。

translations.literal: Because Pi was the eldest, Taizong admired his bearing and treated him with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Because Pi was the eldest, Taizong admired his bearing and treated him with special favor.

sentences.zh: 泰常七年封，拜車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taichang he was enfeoffed and appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taichang he was enfeoffed and appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後督河西、高平諸軍討南秦王楊難當，軍至略陽，禁令齊肅，所過無私，百姓爭致牛酒。

translations.literal: Later he commanded the armies of Hexi and Gaoping against Yang Nandang, Prince of Southern Qin. When the army reached Lueyang, discipline was strict and orderly; wherever it passed there was no private plunder, and the people competed to bring cattle and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Later he commanded the armies of Hexi and Gaoping against Yang Nandang, Prince of Southern Qin. When the army reached Lueyang, discipline was strict and orderly; wherever it passed there was no private plunder, and the people competed to bring cattle and wine.

sentences.zh: 難當懼，還仇池。

translations.literal: Nandang was afraid and returned to Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang was afraid and returned to Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 而諸將議曰，若不誅豪帥，軍還之後，必聚而為寇。

translations.literal: The generals argued, "If we do not execute the powerful leaders, then after the army returns they will surely gather and become bandits."
translations.idiomatic: The generals argued, "If we do not execute the powerful leaders, then after the army returns they will surely gather and become bandits."

sentences.zh: 又以大眾遠出，不有所掠，則無以充軍實，賞將士。

translations.literal: They also reasoned that since the great army had come far, if nothing were seized there would be no way to fill the army stores and reward the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: They also reasoned that since the great army had come far, if nothing were seized there would be no way to fill the army stores and reward the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 將從之。

translations.literal: Pi was about to follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was about to follow this advice.

sentences.zh: 時中書侍郎高允參丕軍事，諫曰：「今若誅之，是傷其向化之心，恐大軍一還，為亂必速。」

translations.literal: At the time Secretariat Attendant Gao Yun was participating in Pi's military affairs. He remonstrated, "If we execute them now, this will wound their will to submit to transformation. I fear that once the great army returns, rebellion will come quickly."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Secretariat Attendant Gao Yun was participating in Pi's military affairs. He remonstrated, "If we execute them now, this will wound their will to submit to transformation. I fear that once the great army returns, rebellion will come quickly."

sentences.zh: 丕以為然，於是綏懷初附，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: Pi considered this right, and so he soothed and embraced those newly attached, without violating so much as an autumn hair.
translations.idiomatic: Pi considered this right, and so he soothed and embraced those newly attached, without violating so much as an autumn hair.

sentences.zh: 初，馮弘之奔高麗，世祖詔遣送之，高麗不遣，世祖怒，將討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Feng Hong fled to Goguryeo, Shizu ordered that he be sent back. Goguryeo did not send him, and Shizu was angry and intended to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Feng Hong fled to Goguryeo, Shizu ordered that he be sent back. Goguryeo did not send him, and Shizu was angry and intended to attack.

sentences.zh: 丕上疏，以為和龍新定，宜優復之，使廣修農殖，以饒軍實，然後進圖，可一舉而滅。

translations.literal: Pi submitted a memorial arguing that Helong had only recently been pacified and should be generously relieved so that farming and planting could be widely restored and military supplies made abundant; only afterward should plans advance, when Goguryeo could be destroyed in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Pi submitted a memorial arguing that Helong had only recently been pacified and should be generously relieved so that farming and planting could be widely restored and military supplies made abundant; only afterward should plans advance, when Goguryeo could be destroyed in one stroke.

sentences.zh: 帝納之，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this and stopped.

sentences.zh: 後坐劉潔事，以憂薨。

translations.literal: Later, implicated in Liu Jie's affair, Pi died of anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Later, implicated in Liu Jie's affair, Pi died of anxiety.

sentences.zh: 事在

translations.literal: The affair is recorded
translations.idiomatic: The affair is recorded

sentences.zh: 〈潔傳〉。

translations.literal: in Jie's biography.
translations.idiomatic: in Jie's biography.

sentences.zh: 諡曰戾王。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Prince Li.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Prince Li.

sentences.zh: 子拔，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Ba succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ba inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 後坐事賜死，國除。

translations.literal: Later, because of an offense, he was ordered to commit suicide, and the fief was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was condemned for a crime and ordered to take his own life, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 丕之薨及日者董道秀之死也，高允遂著筮論曰：「昔明元末起白臺，其高二十餘丈，樂平王嘗夢登其上，四望無所見。

translations.literal: At the death of Pi and the execution of the diviner Dong Daoxiu, Gao Yun thereupon composed a treatise on divination, saying: "In the late reign of Emperor Mingyuan a White Terrace was erected, more than twenty zhang in height. The Prince of Leping once dreamed of climbing it and looking in all four directions, yet saw nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Pi died and the diviner Dong Daoxiu was put to death, Gao Yun wrote a treatise on divination, saying: "Near the end of Emperor Mingyuan's reign a White Terrace was built, more than twenty zhang tall. The Prince of Leping once dreamed that he climbed it and gazed in every direction, yet saw nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 王以問日者董道秀，筮之曰：『大吉。』

translations.literal: The prince asked the diviner Dong Daoxiu about it; Dong divined and said: 'Great good fortune.'
translations.idiomatic: The prince consulted the diviner Dong Daoxiu, who cast the hexagram and declared, 'Great good fortune.'

sentences.zh: 王默而有喜色。

translations.literal: The prince was silent but showed a pleased expression.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said nothing, yet his face showed delight.

sentences.zh: 後事發，王遂憂死，而道秀棄市。

translations.literal: Later the affair came to light; the prince died of grief, and Daoxiu was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter later came to light, the prince died of anxiety, and Daoxiu was executed in the public marketplace.

sentences.zh: 道秀若推六爻以對王曰：『易稱「亢龍有悔」，窮高曰亢，高而無民，不為善也。』

translations.literal: If Daoxiu had analyzed the six lines and replied to the prince, saying: 'The Changes states, "The arrogant dragon will have cause for regret." To reach the extreme of height is called arrogance; to stand high yet without the people is not good.'
translations.idiomatic: Had Daoxiu worked through the six lines and answered the prince, saying, 'The Changes says, "The arrogant dragon will have cause for regret." To press height to the limit is arrogance; to stand aloft without the people beneath one is no blessing,'

sentences.zh: 夫如是，則上寧於王，下保於己，福祿方至，豈有禍哉？

translations.literal: If it had been so, then above he would have secured the prince's peace, and below he would have preserved himself — blessing and emolument would then arrive; how could there have been disaster?
translations.idiomatic: then above he would have reassured the prince, and below he would have kept himself safe; fortune and rank would have followed — how could calamity have come of it?

sentences.zh: 今舍於本而從其末，咎釁之至不亦宜乎！」

translations.literal: Now, having abandoned the root to follow the branch, was it not fitting that blame and calamity should arrive!"
translations.idiomatic: But as it was, he abandoned the root and clung to the branch — was it not only fitting that guilt and disaster should overtake them?"

sentences.zh: 安定王彌，泰常七年封。

translations.literal: Prince Mi of Anding was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mi of Anding was enfeoffed in the seventh year of the Taichang era.

sentences.zh: 太宗討滑臺，留守京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Huatai, he remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong marched against Huatai, he stayed behind to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡殤王。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously styled the Early-Deceased King.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Early-Deceased King.

sentences.zh: 無子，國除。

translations.literal: He had no sons, and the fief was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 樂安王範，泰常七年封。

translations.literal: Fan, Prince of Le'an, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, Prince of Le'an, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.

sentences.zh: 雅性沉厚，寬和仁恕。

translations.literal: His natural character was deep and generous, broad, mild, humane, and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: His natural character was deep and generous, broad, mild, humane, and forgiving.

sentences.zh: 世祖以長安形勝之地，非範莫可任者，乃拜範都督五州諸軍事、衞大將軍、開府儀同三司、長安鎮都大將，高選才能，以為僚佐。

translations.literal: Shizu considered Chang'an a strategically commanding place and believed no one but Fan could be entrusted with it. He therefore appointed Fan commander of military affairs in five provinces, Grand General of the Guards, with an opened office and protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, and grand general of Chang'an Garrison, selecting able men of high quality to serve as his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu considered Chang'an a strategically commanding place and believed no one but Fan could be entrusted with it. He therefore appointed Fan commander of military affairs in five provinces, Grand General of the Guards, with an opened office and protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, and grand general of Chang'an Garrison, selecting able men of high quality to serve as his staff.

sentences.zh: 範謙恭惠下，推心撫納，百姓稱之。

translations.literal: Fan was modest and respectful, kind to those below him, and received and soothed people with open sincerity; the common people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was modest and respectful, kind to those below him, and received and soothed people with open sincerity; the common people praised him.

sentences.zh: 時秦土新罹寇賊，流亡者相繼，範請崇易簡之治，帝納之。

translations.literal: At the time the Qin lands had newly suffered bandits and rebels, and refugees followed one after another. Fan requested that rule there honor ease and simplicity, and the emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Qin lands had newly suffered bandits and rebels, and refugees followed one after another. Fan requested that rule there honor ease and simplicity, and the emperor accepted it.

sentences.zh: 於是遂寬徭，與人休息。

translations.literal: Thereupon corvée was relaxed, and the people were allowed to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon corvée was relaxed, and the people were allowed to rest.

sentences.zh: 後劉潔之謀，範聞而不告。

translations.literal: Later, when Liu Jie plotted, Fan heard of it but did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Liu Jie plotted, Fan heard of it but did not report it.

sentences.zh: 事發，因疾暴薨。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, he suddenly died from illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, he suddenly died from illness.

sentences.zh: 長子良。

translations.literal: His eldest son was Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Liang.

sentences.zh: 世祖未有子，嘗曰：「兄弟之子猶子也。」

translations.literal: Shizu had no son yet and once said: "A brother's son is like one's own son.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu had not yet fathered a son and once said, "A brother's son is as good as one's own."

sentences.zh: 親撫養之。

translations.literal: He personally reared and nurtured him.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Liang himself with fatherly care.

sentences.zh: 長而壯勇多知，常參軍國大計。

translations.literal: When grown, he was bold, brave, and deeply informed, and he regularly took part in great plans of state and army.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he was strong, courageous, and well informed, and he regularly joined in deliberations on matters of state and war.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，襲王。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Gaozong, he inherited the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he inherited the princedom.

sentences.zh: 拜長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史，為內都大官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General of the Capital Garrison of Chang'an and Inspector of Yong Province, and served as Director of the Inner Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand General of the Chang'an Garrison, Inspector of Yong Province, and Director of the Inner Capital.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰簡王。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously styled the Simple King.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Simple King.

sentences.zh: 永昌王健，泰常七年封。

translations.literal: Jian, Prince of Yongchang, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, Prince of Yongchang, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang.

sentences.zh: 健姿貌魁壯，善弓馬，達兵法，所在征戰，常有大功。

translations.literal: Jian was imposing and robust in appearance, skilled with bow and horse, and expert in military methods; wherever he campaigned, he regularly won great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was imposing and robust in appearance, skilled with bow and horse, and expert in military methods; wherever he campaigned, he regularly won great merit.

sentences.zh: 才藝比陳留桓王，而智略過之。

translations.literal: In talent and skill he was comparable to Prince Huan of Chenliu, while in wisdom and strategy he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: In talent and skill he was comparable to Prince Huan of Chenliu, while in wisdom and strategy he surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 從世祖破赫連昌，遂西略至木根山。

translations.literal: He followed Shizu in defeating Helian Chang and then campaigned west as far as Mugen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizu in defeating Helian Chang and then campaigned west as far as Mugen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 討和龍，健別攻拔建德。

translations.literal: During the campaign against Helong, Jian separately attacked and took Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Helong, Jian separately attacked and took Jiande.

sentences.zh: 後平叛胡白龍餘黨于西河。

translations.literal: Later he pacified the remaining followers of the rebel Hu Bailong in Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Later he pacified the remaining followers of the rebel Hu Bailong in Xihe.

sentences.zh: 世祖襲蠕蠕，越涿邪山。

translations.literal: When Shizu made a surprise attack on the Rouran, he crossed Zhuoxie Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu made a surprise attack on the Rouran, he crossed Zhuoxie Mountain.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，詔健殿後，蠕蠕萬騎追之，健與數十騎擊之，矢不虛發，所中皆應弦而斃，遂退。

translations.literal: As the imperial carriage returned, an edict ordered Jian to guard the rear. Ten thousand Rouran cavalry pursued, and Jian struck them with several dozen riders. Not one arrow was loosed in vain; whoever he hit fell dead at the string, and the pursuers withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial carriage returned, an edict ordered Jian to guard the rear. Ten thousand Rouran cavalry pursued, and Jian struck them with several dozen riders. Not one arrow was loosed in vain; whoever he hit fell dead at the string, and the pursuers withdrew.

sentences.zh: 威震漠北。

translations.literal: His awe shook the north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: His awe shook the north of the desert.

sentences.zh: 尋從平涼州，健功居多。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed in pacifying Liangzhou, and Jian's merit was the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he followed in pacifying Liangzhou, and Jian's merit was the greatest.

sentences.zh: 又討破禿髮保周，自殺，傳首京師；

translations.literal: He also attacked and defeated Tufa Baozhou, who killed himself, and Jian sent his head to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked and defeated Tufa Baozhou, who killed himself, and Jian sent his head to the capital;

sentences.zh: 復降沮渠無諱。

translations.literal: he then brought Juqu Wuhui to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: he then brought Juqu Wuhui to surrender.

sentences.zh: 無疾薨，諡曰莊王。

translations.literal: He died without illness and received the posthumous title Prince Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died without illness and received the posthumous title Prince Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子仁，襲。

translations.literal: His son Ren succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ren inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 仁亦驍勇，有父風，世祖奇之。

translations.literal: Ren was also fierce and valiant, having his father's manner; Shizu regarded him with wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Ren was likewise fierce and brave, with his father's bearing, and Shizu took special notice of him.

sentences.zh: 後與濮陽王閭若文謀為不軌，發覺，賜死，國除。

translations.literal: Later he plotted treason with Prince Ruowen of Puyang, Lü Ruowen; when discovered, he was ordered to commit suicide, and the fief was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Later he conspired in treason with Lü Ruowen, Prince of Puyang; when the plot was uncovered he was ordered to take his own life, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 建寧王崇，泰常七年封，拜輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Prince Chong of Jianning was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang and appointed General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chong of Jianning was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang and appointed General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 從討北虜有功。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigns against the northern barbarians and achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in campaigns against the northern foes and won distinction.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，封崇子麗濟南王。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Gaozong, Chong's son Li was enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong, Chong's son Li was enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 後與京兆王杜元寶謀逆，父子並賜死。

translations.literal: Later he plotted rebellion with Prince Yuanbao of Jingzhao, Du Yuanbao; father and son were both ordered to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Later he plotted rebellion with Du Yuanbao, Prince of Jingzhao; father and son were both ordered to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 新興王俊，泰常七年封，拜鎮東大將軍。

translations.literal: Prince Jun of Xinxing was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang and appointed Grand General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun of Xinxing was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Taichang and appointed Grand General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 少善騎射，多才藝。

translations.literal: From youth he was skilled at horsemanship and archery and possessed many talents.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he excelled at riding and archery and had many accomplishments.

sentences.zh: 坐法，削爵為公。

translations.literal: Because of a legal offense, his nobility was reduced and he was made a duke.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted under the law, he was stripped of his princely rank and reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 俊好酒色，多越法度。

translations.literal: Jun was fond of wine and women and often transgressed the laws.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was devoted to wine and women and often overstepped the bounds of law.

sentences.zh: 又以母先遇罪死，而己被貶削，恒懷怨望，頗有悖心。

translations.literal: Moreover, because his mother had previously been condemned and put to death while he himself had been demoted and stripped of rank, he constantly harbored resentment and bore a rebellious heart.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had earlier been condemned and executed, and he himself had been demoted and stripped of rank; he nursed a lasting grievance and came to harbor rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 後事發，賜死，國除。

translations.literal: Later the affair came to light; he was ordered to commit suicide, and the fief was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter later came to light he was ordered to take his own life, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 論曰：樂平、樂安俱以將領自效，竟以憂迫而逝，驗克終之為鮮。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Leping and Le'an both proved themselves as commanders, yet in the end died under anxiety and pressure, showing how rare it is to come to a good end.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Leping and Le'an both proved themselves as commanders, yet in the end died under anxiety and pressure, showing how rare it is to come to a good end.

sentences.zh: 莊王才力智謀，一時之傑，與夫建寧、新興，不同日也。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang, in talent, strength, wisdom, and strategy, was an outstanding man of his age; he cannot be spoken of in the same breath as Jianning and Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhuang, in talent, strength, wisdom, and strategy, was an outstanding man of his age; he cannot be spoken of in the same breath as Jianning and Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷十七 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」，百衲本、汲本、局本卷末有宋人校語云：「魏收書明元六王列傳亡。」

translations.literal: In the table of contents of various editions of the Book of Wei, volume 17 is marked "deficient." At the end of the Baibaina, Ji, and Ju editions, a Song-dynasty collation note states: "Wei Shou's original biography of Emperor Mingyuan's six princes is lost."
translations.idiomatic: The tables of contents in various editions of the Book of Wei mark this volume as deficient. At the end of the Baibaina, Ji, and Ju editions a Song-dynasty collation note reads: "Wei Shou's original biography of Emperor Mingyuan's six princes is lost."

sentences.zh: 殿本考證云：「魏收書亡，後人所補。」

translations.literal: The Dian edition's textual verification states: "Wei Shou's text is lost; later men supplied this."
translations.idiomatic: The Dian edition's textual verification states: "Wei Shou's text is lost; this was supplied by later hands."

sentences.zh: 按此卷以北史卷一六明元六王傳補，間有溢出字句，當出於高氏小史。

translations.literal: This volume was supplemented from the biography of Emperor Mingyuan's six princes in juan 16 of the History of the Northern Dynasties; here and there are superfluous characters and phrases, which likely derive from the Xiaoshi of the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: This volume was restored from the biography of Emperor Mingyuan's six princes in juan 16 of the History of the Northern Dynasties; occasional stray phrases appear that likely come from the Xiaoshi compiled by the Gao family.
